scenarioStory.history: Woke abruptly around 0200 with severe air hunger and a sensation of drowning. Symptoms progressed rapidly over 20-30 minutes. Wife called 911 when he began coughing up pink, frothy sputum and could no longer speak in full sentences. Denies chest pain but reports significant anxiety and a feeling of impending doom. No recent illness, no leg swelling reported prior to tonight by patient (wife notes ankles have looked puffier the past week).
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew finds a 78-year-old male in severe respiratory distress, sitting bolt upright, unable to speak more than 2-3 words at a time, with pink frothy sputum and diffuse crackles. → CPAP and nitro started: Crew applies CPAP with coaching, screens for PDE5 inhibitor use, and administers high-dose sublingual nitroglycerin given the severely elevated blood pressure. → Mask seal maintained continuously: With continuous CPAP and repeated nitroglycerin, the patient's oxygenation, work of breathing, and blood pressure steadily improve during transport.

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew finds a 78-year-old male in severe respiratory distress, sitting bolt upright, unable to speak more than 2-3 words at a time, with pink frothy sputum and diffuse crackles.

scenarioEvents.name: CPAP and nitro started
scenarioEvents.description: Crew applies CPAP with coaching, screens for PDE5 inhibitor use, and administers high-dose sublingual nitroglycerin given the severely elevated blood pressure.
relatedChecklist: Apply CPAP with coaching and reassurance; maintain continuous mask seal
Screen for PDE5 inhibitor use in past 48 hours before administering nitroglycerin
Nitroglycerin 0.8 mg SL, may repeat every 5 minutes while SBP remains greater than 100 mmHg
Place waveform capnography in line to monitor ventilatory status and response to CPAP

scenarioEvents.name: Mask seal maintained continuously
scenarioEvents.description: With continuous CPAP and repeated nitroglycerin, the patient's oxygenation, work of breathing, and blood pressure steadily improve during transport.
relatedChecklist: Maintain continuous CPAP seal through transport; do not remove until ED-ready to switch
Reassess blood pressure before and after each nitroglycerin dose

scenarioEvents.name: CPAP seal broken during transport
scenarioEvents.description: The CPAP mask seal is broken while moving the patient down the stairwell to the ambulance. Positive airway pressure is lost, and the patient rapidly decompensates.
relatedChecklist: Reseal and reapply CPAP mask immediately; do not delay for other interventions

scenarioEvents.name: CPAP and nitro delayed
scenarioEvents.description: The crew spends critical time on history-taking and IV attempts before addressing the airway and oxygenation crisis, allowing the patient to progress toward respiratory failure.
relatedChecklist: Immediately apply CPAP and administer high-dose nitroglycerin now that impending respiratory failure is recognized
